questions.q: What genuinely stays the same between classic ADF pipelines and Fabric pipelines?
options: The orchestration model — activities, control flow, parameters
Nothing at all — Fabric pipelines work completely differently
The dataset object model
The publish step
questions.explain: The core orchestration thinking — activities, control flow like If Condition and ForEach, and parameters — maps directly; what changes is several of the building blocks underneath.

questions.q: How does Fabric handle what used to be a separate dataset object in classic ADF?
options: Connection properties are defined inline, directly inside each activity
Datasets work identically in Fabric with no changes
Fabric requires two separate dataset objects per activity instead of one
Fabric doesn't support any form of dataset configuration
questions.explain: Fabric drops the separate reusable dataset layer entirely — file path, format, and connection are defined inline within the activity itself, like the Copy activity's Source tab.

questions.q: What replaced the explicit Publish step from classic ADF?
options: Save and Run — Save stores your work, Run saves and executes immediately
Publish still exists in Fabric, unchanged
Every pipeline auto-publishes on every edit with no user action
Fabric pipelines can never be saved without running them
questions.explain: Fabric skips the publish step entirely — Save stores your work, and Run saves and executes it right away.

questions.q: How does debugging work differently in Fabric compared to ADF's separate debug mode?
options: There's no separate debug mode — you're always in interactive mode
Fabric requires an even more elaborate debug setup than ADF
Debugging isn't possible at all in Fabric pipelines
Debug mode works identically to ADF, just renamed
questions.explain: Fabric eliminates the distinct debug mode from ADF — there's a single mode, and it's always live/interactive.

questions.q: What real limitation do Connections have compared to ADF's linked services?
options: Connection properties themselves don't support dynamic parameterization the way linked services could
Connections can only be used by a single pipeline each
Connections require a separate Azure subscription
There is no limitation — Connections are strictly more capable in every way
questions.explain: For metadata-driven, parameterized-connection-string patterns, you instead parameterize the connection object a pipeline activity references, since connection properties themselves aren't dynamic.
